### Make global navigation identifiable and keyboard accessible

```yaml
id: T-ea2058ab-c817-4368-9431-b26314f58a2e
priority: 105
status: Ready
parent_pending_ids: ["P-8e0bae93-5539-40e5-b2b7-8b52fd5fbcea"]

relation: main
depends_on: ["T-e2d64818-cd7a-4edb-a8a9-fb345fe1cdd0"]
```

Goal:
Make global navigation identifiable and keyboard accessible.

Current behavior:
MainLayout renders an unnamed menu icon without an expanded-state association or skip link. App FocusOnNavigate targets h1. The audit does not establish a focus-trap defect.

Desired behavior:
Give the menu a meaningful accessible name, expansion state and stable drawer association; add a visible-on-focus skip link to the main landmark. Verify the existing MudBlazor 9.3 drawer behavior before adjusting phone Escape, backdrop dismissal and focus return. Preserve desktop navigation and route focus.

Touch:
- `src/Habitica.WebApp/Layout/MainLayout.razor`
- `src/Habitica.WebApp/App.razor`
- `src/Habitica.WebApp/wwwroot/css/app.css`
- `tests/Habitica.WebApp.Tests/AppNavMenuTests.cs`
- `tests/Habitica.WebApp.Tests/Qualification/SharedLayoutEvidenceTests.cs`

Implementation constraints:
Use actual native or supported pinned component attributes. Avoid inventing a new focus trap or keyboard shortcut conflicting with browser shortcuts. Preserve sign-in and account boundaries.
Use existing application commands and reviewed MCP contracts. Capture any newly discovered browser-only supported agent action as a separate scoped parity bug; presentation changes grant no new execution authority. No live provider mutation, deployment, publication or consent is authorized by processing. Local build/test authorization must be checked against the active implementation instruction and testing.md before execution. Physical devices, assistive technology and hosted qualification remain separate from desktop emulation.

Validation:
Use test-first behavior slices for meaningful interaction or state changes. A layout-only change uses a failing rendered regression rather than a markup-mirroring unit test. The shared qualification task registers ux-ui-rendered-browser and refreshes the profile before any dependent browser check. The audit baseline is research evidence, not fix acceptance. Changed routes require all declared widths, text sizes and light/dark schemes, including obsidian-glow. Browser checks use owned current Release fixtures, isolated synthetic data, bounded readiness/deadlines and verified cleanup; no real account or provider write. Missing required checks block completion.

Acceptance:
- The menu exposes a meaningful name, accurate expanded state and a stable relationship to the controlled drawer.
- Keyboard activation can skip navigation and dismiss the phone drawer with focus returning to a useful visible target.
- Shell navigation, focus indicators and primary content remain usable across the required rendered matrix.

Documentation updates:
Update `.skill-tree/documents/ux-ui-manifest.md` for changed behavior and `.skill-tree/documents/testing.md` for changed qualification contracts. Update `.skill-tree/documents/features.md` when a user flow materially changes. Record exact task-scoped acceptance artifacts and explicit untested paths.
